dimensions.name: Requirements, APIs, and delivery semantics
dimensions.description: Defines notification classes, durable API acceptance, idempotency scope, status semantics, ordering, expiration, and the meaning of delivered for each channel.
strong_indicators: separates accepted, dispatched, provider-accepted, delivered, failed, expired, and cancelled states
treats ambiguous provider timeouts as a reconciliation problem

dimensions.name: Architecture and data model
dimensions.description: Presents coherent ingestion, orchestration, scheduling, channel-delivery, callback, status, and reconciliation paths with durable ownership of state.
evidence_required: atomic handoff from accepted request to asynchronous work
strong_indicators: outbox or equivalent durable publication pattern
separate logical notification, delivery, attempt, and provider observation records
weak_indicators: provider callbacks overwrite state without idempotency or ordering rules

dimensions.name: Capacity, fairness, and cost
dimensions.description: Quantifies fan-out, outage backlog, storage, retry drain rate, provider limits, and tenant fairness under burst traffic.
strong_indicators: bounds noisy tenants and explains backlog-drain headroom
weak_indicators: no numerical estimate for fan-out or outage storage

dimensions.name: Reliability and recovery
dimensions.description: Handles database, queue, provider, webhook, and regional failures without silent loss or uncontrolled duplicate user-visible sends.
strong_indicators: bounded retries with expiration and operator replay controls
periodic reconciliation against provider message IDs
source-of-truth and conflict rules remain clear during failover
weak_indicators: DLQ without inspection and idempotent replay

dimensions.name: Security, privacy, and residency
dimensions.description: Defines tenant isolation, credential boundaries, payload encryption/redaction, administrative audit, and enforceable EU data-residency controls.
strong_indicators: payloads and recipient addresses are excluded from routine logs
EU payloads remain in approved regions while global metadata is minimized
weak_indicators: global payload replication despite residency requirement
shared provider credentials exposed to tenant-facing services

dimensions.name: Observability, operations, and migration
dimensions.description: Defines measurable SLOs, bounded-cardinality telemetry, reconciliation and DLQ operations, and a reversible migration from the synchronous sender.
evidence_required: acceptance, queue-age, delivery-latency, failure, and reconciliation metrics
strong_indicators: shadow or dual-path comparison before cutover
separates provider degradation from worker, database, and tenant-pressure signals
weak_indicators: big-bang migration without correctness comparison or rollback

score_bands.90-100: Complete quantified design with explicit delivery semantics, durable recovery, tenant fairness, residency boundaries, and a reversible migration.
score_bands.75-89: Strong core architecture with one material gap in capacity, failover, provider reconciliation, or operations.
score_bands.60-74: Plausible baseline that remains underspecified for duplicate delivery, overload, regional failure, or tenant isolation.
score_bands.0-59: Technology list or happy-path queue design that cannot satisfy durability, scale, or isolation requirements.
